title: Spontaneous pneumothorax (BTS 2023)
stem: Teaching room. Your junior has just seen a 22-year-old tall, thin man who smokes, with sudden right-sided chest pain and mild breathlessness. SpO2 97%, HR 88, BP 124/76. The chest X-ray is on the board. Teach the junior how to manage him.

phases.title: Teach the plan
phases.goal: BTS 2023: symptoms and high-risk features, not size; then teach-back.

review.text: Size-based management. Your notes use BTS 2010: observe if under 2 cm and asymptomatic, aspirate if over 2 cm. BTS 2023 decides by symptoms, high-risk features and the patient's priorities: a minimally symptomatic primary pneumothorax can be managed conservatively whatever its size; a symptomatic one gets an ambulatory device or needle aspiration, and a drain if these fail.

notes:
Checked against the British Thoracic Society Guideline for Pleural Disease (2023).

BTS 2023 changed management from size-based to symptom-based. Primary spontaneous pneumothorax (PSP): if minimally symptomatic and the patient agrees, conservative management (outpatient review) is an option regardless of size; if symptomatic (and high-risk features absent), consider ambulatory devices or needle aspiration; chest drain if these fail. High-risk characteristics: haemodynamic compromise, significant hypoxia, bilateral, underlying lung disease (secondary pneumothorax), age over 50 with smoking, haemopneumothorax. Secondary pneumothorax: usually admission and a drain or aspiration. Size is measured at the hilum (inter-pleural distance); 2 cm roughly equals 50% volume but now matters less than symptoms. Needle aspiration site: 2nd intercostal space mid-clavicular line, or 4th–5th space in the safe triangle. Advice: stop smoking, no diving ever unless definitive surgery, no flying until resolved on X-ray (airlines often ask for 1–2 weeks after resolution).

Your notes use the older BTS 2010 approach: observe if under 2 cm and asymptomatic, aspirate if over 2 cm. BTS 2023 manages by symptoms and patient priorities instead. The aspiration technique and discharge advice in your notes match.

Perfect script checked against BTS 2023, a teaching checklist, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the wrong options and unhelpful replies; added a teach-back close.

script.say: That was BTS 2010. The 2023 guideline treats by symptoms, not size: if he's minimally symptomatic and has no high-risk features, conservative outpatient care is an option even for a large one.
The film: a visceral pleural line with no lung markings beyond it, a 3 cm rim measured at the hilum, no mediastinal shift.
First, high-risk features: unstable, hypoxic, bilateral, underlying lung disease making it secondary, over 50 and a smoker, or a haemopneumothorax. He has none.

Then: is he symptomatic, and what are his priorities? Minimal symptoms: conservative, review in 2 to 4 days with a repeat film. Symptomatic: needle aspiration or an ambulatory device; a chest drain if they fail.
Advice: stop smoking, no flying until it's resolved on the film, never dive unless he has definitive surgery, and come back if he's breathless.
Teach-back: you tell me: what decides the plan now, and what will you offer him?
script.do: Symptoms and high-risk features, not size; conservative or aspiration; flying, diving, smoking.
